title: The Ass and His Driver
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: An Ass was being driven down a mountain road, and after jogging along for a while sensibly enough he suddenly quitted the track and rushed to the edge of a precipice. He was just about to leap over the edge when his Driver caught hold of his tail and did his best to pull him back: but pull as he might he couldn't get the Ass to budge from the brink. At last he gave up, crying, "All right, then, get to the bottom your own way; but it's the way to sudden death, as you'll find out quick enough."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where was the Ass being driven?
options: Down a mountain road
Through a busy market
Along a riverbank
Across an open field

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how was the Ass behaving before he suddenly changed course?
options: Jogging along sensibly enough
Refusing to move at all
Braying loudly at every step
Straining against his harness

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Ass suddenly do?
options: Quitted the track and rushed to the edge of a precipice
Lay down and refused to continue
Turned around and headed back uphill
Threw off his load and ran into the forest

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Driver do when the Ass rushed to the edge?
options: Caught hold of his tail and tried to pull him back
Shouted at him from a distance
Ran ahead to block his path
Let go of the reins and stepped away

questions.prompt: According to the passage, was the Driver able to move the Ass from the brink?
options: No, he couldn't get the Ass to budge
Yes, after a long struggle
Yes, almost immediately
The passage does not say whether he succeeded

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Driver finally tell the Ass to do?
options: Get to the bottom his own way
Wait until another driver arrives
Turn back the way they came
Rest until he calms down

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Driver's final warning suggest about the outcome he expects for the Ass?
options: He believes the Ass is heading toward his own destruction by refusing to be pulled back
He believes the Ass will find a safer path on his own
He expects the Ass to change his mind at the very last moment
He thinks the Ass is only pretending to be stubborn

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Stubbornly refusing good guidance can leave someone to face a danger they brought upon themselves
Drivers should never try to guide an animal that resists them
Mountain roads are too dangerous for asses to travel
Sudden changes in behavior are always a sign of fear

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Ass about to do at the edge of the precipice?
options: Leap over the edge
Turn back on his own
Call out for help
Stand still and refuse to move further

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what part of the Ass did the Driver grab hold of?
options: His tail
His mane
His harness
His ear

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Driver call the path to sudden death?
options: "The way" the Ass is now taking
A shortcut the Ass invented himself
A path only foolish animals use
A route the Driver had warned him about before

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Driver eventually let go of the Ass despite trying his best to save him?
options: He realizes the Ass's own stubbornness leaves him no way left to help
He decides the Ass does not deserve to be saved
He is called away by an emergency elsewhere
He believes the precipice is not truly dangerous after all

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "brink" mean in "budge from the brink"?
options: The very edge of a steep or dangerous drop
A narrow path through a forest
A rope used to lead an animal
The bottom of a valley

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: An Ass suddenly rushes toward a precipice, and when his Driver cannot pull him back, he warns the Ass of the deadly fate awaiting him
An Ass and his Driver work together to avoid a dangerous precipice
A Driver pushes an Ass over a precipice on purpose
An Ass refuses to walk down a mountain road at all
